workflow_rationale: Adding cross-platform support to a new OS (Linux) with multiple distribution formats. Follows the typical feature workflow: configuration → implementation → CI/CD → integration testing.

phases.name: Packaging Configuration
phases.description: Configure electron-builder for Snap packaging and enhance Linux-specific settings

subtasks.description: Add Snap target to electron-builder.yml configuration
subtasks.notes: Add snap target with classic confinement (required for DuckDB file access). Include desktop file metadata and icon paths.

subtasks.description: Enhance Linux category and metadata in electron-builder.yml
subtasks.notes: Added desktop file configuration with proper categories (Office;Finance;Development), keywords (aws;cloud;cost;billing;finops;analytics), GenericName, Comment, and StartupWMClass for proper Linux desktop integration. Verification passed - desktop: configuration exists in electron-builder.yml.

phases.name: XDG Directory Support
phases.description: Implement XDG Base Directory specification for Linux config and data paths

subtasks.notes: Created XDG path resolver utility with platform detection. Implements XDG Base Directory specification for Linux ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME, $XDG_DATA_HOME with proper fallbacks to ~/.config and ~/.local/share). Returns standard paths for macOS/Windows. TypeScript compilation and ESLint verification passed.

subtasks.description: Integrate XDG paths into main process
subtasks.notes: Integrated XDG paths into main process. Imported resolveConfigDir and resolveDataDir from xdg-paths module. Config and data directories now use XDG Base Directory specification on Linux (~/.config/CostGoblin and ~/.local/share/CostGoblin) while maintaining backward compatibility on macOS/Windows. Environment variables still override default paths. TypeScript compilation and ESLint verification passed.

phases.name: Linux Desktop Integration
phases.description: Implement tray icon and native notifications for Linux desktop environments

subtasks.notes: Created tray-manager.ts following update-manager.ts patterns. Implemented initTray() with Tray, Menu, and nativeImage from Electron. Context menu provides Show/Hide CostGoblin and Quit options. Tray click toggles window visibility. Integrated in main.ts with Linux platform detection. Updated window-all-closed handler to keep app running on Linux when tray is active. Verification passed - TypeScript compilation, ESLint, and all tests passed.

Created notification-manager.ts following update-manager.ts patterns. Implemented showNotification() with Electron Notification API supporting Windows, macOS, and Linux (GNOME, KDE). Added notification functions: notifySyncComplete, notifySyncError, notifyUpdateAvailable, notifyUpdateDownloaded. Integrated into update-manager.ts for update events and handlers/sync.ts for sync completion/error events. Notifications respect OS-level notification settings. All TypeScript compilation, ESLint, and tests passed.

subtasks.description: Add tray icon PNG assets for Linux

verification.command: test -f build/tray-icon.png && file build/tray-icon.png | grep -q PNG

subtasks.notes: Created tray icon PNG assets for Linux. Generated tray-icon.png (22x22) and tray-icon@2x.png (44x44) from the main icon.png using PIL/Pillow. Standard sizes for Linux tray icons following GNOME and KDE guidelines. Verification passed - both PNG files created successfully.

phases.name: CI/CD Updates
phases.description: Update GitHub Actions workflows to build and verify Linux packages

subtasks.description: Add Linux arm64 build to release workflow
subtasks.notes: Added linux/arm64 matrix entry to release.yml workflow. Both x64 and arm64 architectures will now be built for Linux releases using ubuntu-latest runner. Verification passed - grep confirms arm64 configuration in Linux builds.

subtasks.description: Add Linux package verification to CI

verification.expected: Exit code 0 (Linux build step in CI)

subtasks.notes: Added verify-linux-packages job to CI workflow. Runs on ubuntu-latest with Node.js 24. Executes 'npx electron-builder --linux --dir' in packages/desktop to verify Linux packaging builds successfully. The --dir flag builds unpacked directory for faster verification without creating full distributable packages. Verification passed.

phases.name: Integration Testing
phases.description: Manual verification of Linux packages on Ubuntu and Fedora

subtasks.description: Build and test all Linux packages locally

verification.instructions:
1. Run 'npx electron-builder --linux' to build all formats
2. Verify dist/ contains .AppImage, .deb, and .snap files
3. Check file sizes are reasonable (AppImage ~150-200MB)
4. Verify DuckDB native module is included in packages

subtasks.notes: Local build verification completed. Added required metadata to package.json (description, author) and fixed electron version for electron-builder. Unpacked Linux directory builds successfully (331MB). Snap metadata generated correctly. Note: Final .AppImage, .deb, .snap packages require Linux environment - CI builds on ubuntu-latest will create them. DuckDB configured to unpack from asar correctly.

verification.instructions:
1. Copy .AppImage to Ubuntu 22.04 VM
2. Make executable: chmod +x CostGoblin-*.AppImage
3. Run: ./CostGoblin-*.AppImage
4. Verify app launches and DuckDB queries work
5. Check tray icon appears
6. Test notification display
7. Verify config saved to ~/.config/CostGoblin or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME
8. Verify data saved to ~/.local/share/CostGoblin or $XDG_DATA_HOME

subtasks.notes: Created comprehensive testing guide (ubuntu-22.04-appimage-test-guide.md) with 10 test cases covering: basic execution, DuckDB functionality, tray icon, notifications, XDG directory compliance, persistence, multi-instance prevention, auto-update, desktop integration, and performance. Includes automated test script and troubleshooting guide. Manual testing requires Ubuntu 22.04 environment with built AppImage from Linux CI - Windows environment cannot create final AppImage packages. Testing guide ready for QA team.

verification.instructions:
1. Install: sudo dpkg -i costgoblin_*.deb
2. Resolve dependencies if needed: sudo apt-get install -f
3. Launch from applications menu
4. Verify desktop file integration (icon, launcher)
5. Test same functionality as AppImage
6. Uninstall: sudo apt remove costgoblin

subtasks.notes: Created comprehensive testing guide (ubuntu-22.04-deb-test-guide.md) with 15 test cases covering: package installation, desktop integration, file system layout, application launch, DuckDB functionality, tray icon, notifications, XDG directory compliance, persistence, multi-instance prevention, package dependencies, system updates, uninstallation, auto-update (N/A for .deb), and performance. Includes automated test script (ubuntu-22.04-deb-test.sh) for package validation. Manual testing requires Ubuntu 22.04 environment with built .deb from Linux CI - Windows environment cannot create final .deb packages. Testing guide ready for QA team. Covers .deb-specific aspects: apt/dpkg integration, dependency resolution, proper Debian filesystem hierarchy, and package management lifecycle.

verification.instructions:
1. Copy .AppImage to Fedora 39 VM
2. Make executable and run
3. Verify app works on RPM-based distro
4. Test with KDE Plasma desktop environment (if available)
5. Verify tray icon compatibility with KDE

subtasks.notes: Created comprehensive testing guide (fedora-39-test-guide.md) with 12 test cases covering: basic execution, DuckDB functionality, tray icon on KDE Plasma, tray icon on GNOME, native notifications, XDG directory compliance, application persistence, multi-instance prevention, Wayland compatibility, SELinux compatibility, performance, and desktop integration. Includes automated test script (fedora-39-test.sh) for system validation. Manual testing requires Fedora 39 environment (Workstation or KDE Spin) with built AppImage from Linux CI - Windows environment cannot create final AppImage packages. Testing guide ready for QA team. Covers Fedora-specific aspects: RPM ecosystem, KDE Plasma integration, Wayland session, SELinux enforcing mode, and system library compatibility.

verification.instructions:
1. Launch CostGoblin from AppImage
2. Check Help > Check for Updates menu
3. Verify update check works (may show 'up to date')
4. Note: Snap updates handled by Snap Store automatically
5. Note: .deb updates require manual download or repository setup

subtasks.notes: AppImage supports delta updates via electron-updater. Snap has built-in auto-update. .deb requires repository or manual updates.

parallel_groups.reason: Both are independent implementation tasks with no file conflicts

parallelism.speedup_estimate: Minimal parallelism benefit due to sequential dependencies in later phases

summary.startup_command: npm run check && npm run build --workspace=packages/desktop

acceptance_criteria: All three Linux package formats (AppImage, deb, Snap) build successfully
Packages install and run on Ubuntu 22.04+ and Fedora 39+
DuckDB native module works on Linux x64 and ARM64
Tray icon displays on GNOME and KDE
Native notifications work on Linux desktop environments
File paths follow XDG Base Directory specification
CI builds and verifies Linux packages on every PR
All existing tests pass on Linux

verification_steps.name: Linux Package Build
verification_steps.expected_outcome: AppImage, deb, and snap packages created in dist/

verification_strategy.reasoning: Medium risk change adding platform support. Requires unit tests for new code, integration testing for packaging, and manual verification on target Linux distributions. No security scanning needed as this is platform packaging, not security-critical code.

checks: AppImage launches and runs on Ubuntu 22.04
Config files saved to XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config
Data files saved to XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share
